questions.q: The entities listed under inflammatory bowel disease are:
opts: Ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease, microscopic colitis and diversion colitis
Ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease only
Microscopic colitis and collagenous colitis only
questions.exp: Entities of inflammatory bowel disease: 1. ulcerative colitis (UC), 2. Crohn's disease (CD), 3. microscopic colitis, 4. diversion colitis. (Book p30)

questions.q: The book states that currently inflammatory bowel disease includes only:
questions.exp: Currently, inflammatory bowel disease includes only UC and CD. (Book p30)

questions.q: Microscopic colitis is associated with long-term use of:
questions.exp: Microscopic colitis: associated with long-term use of PPI and NSAIDS. (Book p30)

questions.q: Microscopic colitis presents with:
opts: Chronic, non-bloody, voluminous, watery diarrhea similar to small bowel diarrhea
Small volume bloody diarrhea with tenesmus
questions.exp: Microscopic colitis: chronic, non-bloody, voluminous, watery diarrhea (similar to small bowel diarrhea). (Book p30)

questions.q: Clinical examination in microscopic colitis is:
questions.exp: Microscopic colitis: on clinical examination — normal. (Book p30)

questions.q: Endoscopy in microscopic colitis is:
questions.exp: Microscopic colitis investigations: endoscopy — normal. (Book p30)

questions.q: Match the microscopic colitis pattern to its printed feature — 1) Collagenous colitis 2) Lymphocytic colitis … A) Intra-epithelial lymphocytes B) Collagen band in mucosa
questions.exp: Biopsy: collagenous colitis — collagen band in mucosa; lymphocytic colitis — intra-epithelial lymphocytes. (Book p30)

questions.q: Match the microscopic colitis pattern to its printed association — 1) Collagenous colitis 2) Lymphocytic colitis … A) Celiac disease B) Sjogren's syndrome
questions.exp: Collagenous colitis is associated with Sjogren's syndrome; lymphocytic colitis with celiac disease. (Book p30)

questions.q: An elderly patient on long-term PPI has chronic watery voluminous non-bloody diarrhea with a normal colonoscopy. The book's diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Microscopic colitis: long-term PPI and NSAIDS, chronic non-bloody voluminous watery diarrhea with normal endoscopy. (Book p30)

questions.sec: Diversion Colitis & Normal Histology of Colon
questions.q: Diversion colitis is seen in:
opts: Patients using colostomy bags after surgery for bowel malignancies
Patients with ileostomy for ulcerative colitis only
questions.exp: Diversion colitis: colitis seen in patients using colostomy bags (after surgery for bowel malignancies). (Book p30)

questions.sec: Diversion Colitis & Normal Histology of Colon
questions.q: Order the layers of the normal colon as printed, innermost to outermost — 1) Mucosal epithelial cells 2) Lamina propria 3) Muscularis mucosa 4) Submucosa 5) Muscularis propria 6) Serosa … A) Serosa B) Mucosal epithelial cells C) Submucosa D) Lamina propria E) Muscularis propria F) Muscularis mucosa
questions.exp: Normal histology of colon, innnermost to outermost: mucosal epithelial cells, lamina propria, muscularis mucosa, submucosa, muscularis propria, serosa. (Book p30)

questions.sec: Diversion Colitis & Normal Histology of Colon
questions.q: In the printed layer list, the layer immediately outside the muscularis mucosa is the:
questions.exp: Layers: mucosal epithelial cells → lamina propria → muscularis mucosa → submucosa → muscularis propria → serosa. (Book p30)

questions.sec: Diversion Colitis & Normal Histology of Colon
questions.q: Pick the ODD ONE OUT — one is not a printed layer of the normal colon:
questions.exp: The printed layers are mucosal epithelial cells, lamina propria, muscularis mucosa, submucosa, muscularis propria and serosa. Adventitia is not listed. (Book p30)

questions.q: Compared with the small intestine, the colonic mucosa has:
questions.exp: Mucosa: villi are absent in the colon. (Book p31)

questions.q: The crypts of the colon contain microvilli whose function is:
questions.exp: Crypts: contain microvilli — water absorption. (Book p31)

questions.q: Goblet cells of the colon:
questions.exp: Goblet cells: secrete mucus. (Book p31)

questions.q: The note defines diarrhea as a stool volume above:
questions.exp: Note: diarrhea → >200 mL of stool volume. (Book p31)

questions.sec: Epidemiology of UC and Crohn's Disease
questions.q: Overall, in the epidemiology of IBD:
opts: CD is more common than UC, and males outnumber females
UC is more common than CD, and females outnumber males
UC and CD are equally common
CD is more common but females outnumber males
questions.exp: Epidemiology overall: CD > UC; males > females. (Book p31)

questions.sec: Epidemiology of UC and Crohn's Disease
questions.q: Match the epidemiological variable to the printed UC and CD values — 1) Female:male ratio 2) Smoking 3) Appendicectomy 4) OCP … A) UC protective / CD no association B) UC males > females / CD females > males (OCP use) C) UC no increased risk / CD increased risk D) UC protective / CD causative
questions.exp: Female:male ratio — UC males > females, CD females > males (OCP use); smoking — UC protective, CD causative; appendicectomy — UC protective, CD no association; OCP — UC no increased risk, CD increased risk. (Book p31)

questions.sec: Epidemiology of UC and Crohn's Disease
questions.q: Smoking in IBD is:
opts: Protective for UC and causative for CD
Causative for UC and protective for CD
questions.exp: Smoking: UC — protective; CD — causative. (Book p31)

questions.sec: Epidemiology of UC and Crohn's Disease
questions.q: Appendicectomy is:
opts: Protective for UC with no association for CD
questions.exp: Appendicectomy: UC — protective; CD — no association. (Book p31)

questions.sec: Epidemiology of UC and Crohn's Disease
questions.q: Oral contraceptive pills carry:
opts: Increased risk for CD but no increased risk for UC
Increased risk for UC but not CD
questions.exp: OCP: UC — no increased risk; CD — increased risk. (Book p31)

questions.sec: Epidemiology of UC and Crohn's Disease
questions.q: Familial inheritance (concordance) in IBD is:
opts: Significant, and greater for CD than UC
Significant and greater for UC than CD
questions.exp: Familial inheritance (concordance): significant; CD > UC. (Book p31)

questions.sec: Epidemiology of UC and Crohn's Disease
questions.q: Antibiotics in the first year of life increase the risk of IBD by:
questions.exp: Antibiotics in 1st year of life → increases risk of IBD by 3 times. (Book p31)

questions.sec: Epidemiology of UC and Crohn's Disease
questions.q: The age distribution of IBD is described by the book as having peaks at:
questions.exp: Age: peaks at 15-30 years and 70-90 years. (Book p31)

questions.sec: Epidemiology of UC and Crohn's Disease
questions.q: The ethnicity gradient listed for IBD runs:
opts: Jews > non-Jewish white > African American > Hispanic > Asian
Asian > Hispanic > African American > non-Jewish white > Jews
African American > non-Jewish white > Jews > Hispanic > Asian
Non-Jewish white > Jews > Hispanic > Asian > African American
questions.exp: Ethnicity: Jews > non-Jewish white > African American > Hispanic > Asian. (Book p31)

questions.sec: Epidemiology of UC and Crohn's Disease
questions.q: Behcet's disease and Crohn's disease share a common antibody, namely:
questions.exp: Note: Behcet's disease has GI manifestations like Crohn's disease and shares a common antibody — ASCA. (Book p31)

questions.sec: Epidemiology of UC and Crohn's Disease
questions.q: Prolonged use of which drug causes features similar to ulcerative colitis?
questions.exp: Note: prolonged use of α-methyl dopa causes features similar to ulcerative colitis. (Book p31)

questions.sec: Epidemiology of UC and Crohn's Disease
questions.q: A patient develops a UC-like colitis after long-term therapy for hypertension. The drug implicated in the note is:
questions.exp: Prolonged use of α-methyl dopa causes features similar to ulcerative colitis. (Book p31)

questions.sec: Epidemiology of UC and Crohn's Disease
questions.q: Campylobacter jejuni is noted as a risk factor for IBD and also causes:
opts: Large bowel diarrhea and Guillain Barre syndrome
Small bowel diarrhea and hemolytic uremic syndrome
questions.exp: Campylobacter jejuni is a risk factor for IBD (also causes large bowel diarrhea, Guillain Barre syndrome). (Book p31)

questions.q: Match the syndrome to its printed defect or inheritance — 1) Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome 2) Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome 3) Von Gierke's disease … A) Glucose-1-phosphatase deficiency B) WASP gene mutation (X-linked recessive) C) Autosomal recessive
questions.exp: Wiskott-Aldrich — WASP gene mutation (X-linked recessive); Hermansky-Pudlak — autosomal recessive; von Gierke's disease (glycogen storage disorder type I) — glucose-1-phosphatase deficiency. (Book p32)

questions.q: The triad of Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome is:
opts: Recurrent sino-pulmonary infections, recurrent eczema and recurrent thrombocytopenia with microplatelets
Recurrent infections, albinism and pulmonary fibrosis
questions.exp: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome: triad of 1. recurrent sino-pulmonary infections, 2. recurrent eczema, 3. recurrent thrombocytopenia (microplatelets). (Book p32)

questions.q: The platelet abnormality in Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome is:
opts: Platelet dysfunction with a normal count
questions.exp: Wiskott-Aldrich: recurrent thrombocytopenia (microplatelets). (Book p32)

questions.q: Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome is characterised by:
opts: Platelet dysfunction with a normal platelet count
Normal platelets and normal bleeding time
questions.exp: Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome: platelet dysfunction with normal platelet count. (Book p32)

questions.q: The interstitial lung disease of Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome is:
questions.exp: Hermansky-Pudlak: interstitial lung disease — pulmonary fibrosis. (Book p32)

questions.q: The third feature of Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome is:
questions.exp: Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome: oculocutaneous albinism. (Book p32)

questions.q: The features listed for von Gierke's disease are:
opts: Hypoglycemia with or without seizures and Doll facies, hepatomegaly, lactic acidosis, hyperuricemia and hyperlipidemia
Hypoglycemia, jaundice and renal tubular acidosis
questions.exp: Von Gierke's disease features: hypoglycemia ± seizures, Doll facies; hepatomegaly; lactic acidosis; hyperuricemia; hyperlipidemia. (Book p32)

questions.q: Von Gierke's disease is glycogen storage disorder type ____.
questions.exp: Von Gierke's disease (glycogen storage disorder — type I). (Book p32)

questions.q: Syndromes presenting as IBD in childhood are grouped as:
questions.exp: Present as IBD in childhood: UC (non-granulomatous) versus CD (granulomatous). (Book p32)

questions.q: The syndrome the book lists as the most common (m/c) presenting as IBD in childhood is:
questions.exp: Genetic syndromes associated with IBD: Turner's syndrome — m/c. (Book p32)

questions.q: Pick the ODD ONE OUT — one is not a listed genetic syndrome associated with IBD:
questions.exp: Listed syndromes: Turner's syndrome (m/c), Wiskott-Aldrich, Hermansky-Pudlak and von Gierke's disease. Marfan syndrome is not listed. (Book p32)

questions.sec: IPEX Syndrome & Early Onset Childhood IBD
questions.q: IPEX syndrome stands for:
questions.exp: IPEX: immune polyendocrinopathy X-linked syndrome. (Book p32)

questions.sec: IPEX Syndrome & Early Onset Childhood IBD
questions.q: IPEX results from loss of ____ function causing reduced regulatory T-cell tolerance.
questions.exp: Pathology: loss of Foxp3 function → reduced T-reg cell tolerance → IPEX syndrome. (Book p32)

questions.sec: IPEX Syndrome & Early Onset Childhood IBD
questions.q: The triad of IPEX syndrome is:
opts: Dermatitis, endocrinopathy (type I DM / thyroiditis) and UC-like enteropathy
questions.exp: IPEX clinical features: triad of dermatitis, endocrinopathy (type I DM / thyroiditis), UC-like enteropathy. (Book p32)

questions.sec: IPEX Syndrome & Early Onset Childhood IBD
questions.q: Management of IPEX syndrome is:
opts: Supportive care and replacement therapy, and gene therapy
questions.exp: IPEX management: supportive care and replacement therapy; gene therapy. (Book p33)

questions.sec: IPEX Syndrome & Early Onset Childhood IBD
questions.q: The investigation for IPEX syndrome is:
questions.exp: IPEX investigations: genetic testing. (Book p33)

questions.sec: IPEX Syndrome & Early Onset Childhood IBD
questions.q: Match the T-cell marker to its printed meaning — 1) CD3 2) CD25 3) CD4 … A) Helper T-cell B) Pan T-cell marker C) T-reg cell
questions.exp: Markers of T-reg cell: CD3 — pan T-cell marker; CD25 — T-reg cell; CD4 — helper T-cell. (Book p33)

questions.sec: IPEX Syndrome & Early Onset Childhood IBD
questions.q: Early onset childhood IBD is associated with a defect in:
questions.exp: Early onset childhood IBD: defect in IL-10 or IL-10 receptor function. (Book p33)

questions.sec: IPEX Syndrome & Early Onset Childhood IBD
questions.q: Early onset childhood IBD presents as:
opts: Severe refractory IBD in early life
questions.exp: Early onset childhood IBD: severe refractory IBD in early life. (Book p33)

questions.sec: IPEX Syndrome & Early Onset Childhood IBD
questions.q: The most potent anti-inflammatory cytokine in the body, per the note, is:
questions.exp: Note: most potent anti-inflammatory cytokine in the body — IL-10. (Book p33)

questions.q: Exogenous and endogenous factors produce a dysregulated ____ immune response in a genetically susceptible individual.
questions.exp: Pathogenesis of IBD: exogenous and endogenous factors → dysregulated mucosal immune response in a genetically susceptible individual. (Book p33)

questions.q: In ulcerative colitis the overactive adaptive immune system is described as which lineage?
questions.exp: Ulcerative colitis: overactive adaptive immune system — Th2 lineage. (Book p33)

questions.q: The gene polymorphism linked to Crohn's disease is:
questions.exp: Crohn's disease: NOD2 (CARD15) gene polymorphism on chromosome 16 in genetically susceptible individuals. (Book p33)

questions.q: Defective innate immunity in Crohn's disease includes decreased clearance of:
opts: Intracellular organisms — Mycobacterium paratuberculosis and M. avium complex
questions.exp: Defective innate immunity: decreased clearance of intracellular organisms (Mycobacterium paratuberculosis, M. avium complex). (Book p33)

questions.q: Another innate defect listed for Crohn's disease is:
opts: Decreased defensin production from Paneth cells
Increased defensin production from Paneth cells
Paneth cell metaplasia in the rectum
questions.exp: Defective innate immunity: decreased defensin production from Paneth cells. (Book p33)

questions.q: Match the Crohn's disease pathogenic step to its printed content — 1) Defective innate immunity 2) Defective autophagy 3) Overactive adaptive immunity 4) Altered microbiota … A) Decrease in gut bacteria like Faecalibacterium (gut protective) B) Decreased clearance of intracellular organisms C) Th1 lineage D) Autophagy defect
questions.exp: Defective innate immunity: decreased clearance of intracellular organisms and decreased defensin from Paneth cells; defective autophagy; overactive adaptive immune system (Th1 lineage); decrease in protective gut bacteria such as Faecalibacterium. (Book p33)

questions.q: The protective gut bacterium noted as decreased in Crohn's disease is:
questions.exp: Decrease in gut bacteria like Faecalibacterium (gut protective). (Book p33)

questions.q: TRUE or FALSE — the book attributes the adaptive immune overactivity of Crohn's disease to the Th1 lineage.
opts: True — Th1 lineage in Crohn's disease
False — Crohn's disease is Th2 mediated
False — the lineage is not identified
True — but Th2 is also overactive
questions.exp: Overactive adaptive immune system (Th lineage: Crohn's disease) — Th1. (Book p33)

questions.q: The rectum alone is the site of involvement in ulcerative colitis in what proportion?
questions.exp: Site of involvement — ulcerative colitis: rectum alone 50%. (Book p34)

questions.q: The macroscopy of ulcerative colitis is described as:
opts: Hemorrhagic, edematous, ulcerated mucosa with a granular surface
Normal mucosa with patchy skip lesions
questions.exp: Macroscopy: hemorrhagic, edematous, ulcerated mucosa with granular surface. (Book p34)

questions.q: Pseudopolyps in ulcerative colitis are inflammatory polyps due to epithelial ____.
questions.exp: Pseudopolyps: inflammatory polyp d/t epithelial regeneration. (Book p34)

questions.q: The lead pipe appearance of the colon is:
opts: Atrophic and featureless, seen in chronic long-standing UC (rare)
The typical finding of acute severe UC
questions.exp: Chronic long-standing UC (rare): lead pipe appearance (atrophic, featureless colon). (Book p34)

questions.q: Match the lead pipe features as printed — 1) Feature a 2) Feature b … A) Shortening and narrowing of colon B) Loss of haustrations
questions.exp: Lead pipe appearance: a. loss of haustrations; b. shortening and narrowing of colon. (Book p34)

questions.q: Toxic megacolon in fulminant colitis is defined by a colon diameter above:
questions.exp: Fulminant colitis (very rare): toxic megacolon (colon diameter >6 cm). (Book p34)

questions.q: Fulminant colitis with toxic megacolon is described as:
questions.exp: Fulminant colitis (very rare): toxic megacolon (colon diameter >6 cm). (Book p34)

questions.q: Haustrations in the uninvolved colon in ulcerative colitis are:
questions.exp: Image label: haustrations present (uninvolved colon). (Book p34)

questions.q: A barium study in long-standing UC shows an atrophic, featureless, shortened colon without haustrations. The book calls this:
questions.exp: Lead pipe appearance (atrophic, featureless colon) with loss of haustrations and shortening, seen on barium study. (Book p34)

questions.q: The microscopic description of ulcerative colitis begins with:
opts: Cryptitis with loss of crypt architecture
questions.exp: Microscopy: cryptitis with loss of crypt architecture. (Book p35)

questions.q: Paneth cell metaplasia in ulcerative colitis is seen:
questions.exp: Paneth cell metaplasia (seen distal to hepatic flexure). (Book p35)

questions.q: The earliest microscopic finding in ulcerative colitis is:
opts: Basal plasma cells and lymphoid aggregates
questions.exp: Basal plasma cell and lymphoid aggregates: earliest finding. (Book p35)

questions.q: Basal plasma cells are useful because they:
opts: Can help in diagnosing relapse in patients in remission
questions.exp: Basal plasma cell and lymphoid aggregates: earliest finding; can help in diagnosing relapse in remission patients. (Book p35)

questions.q: All of the following are listed as factors AGAINST the diagnosis of ulcerative colitis EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Factors against UC: transmural involvement, thickening, fistulas, fibrosis, skip lesions, strictures, deep ulcers, fissures, abscess. Continuous mucosal involvement is typical of UC. (Book p35)

questions.q: Match the finding to the disease it argues against or for — 1) Skip lesions 2) Cryptitis with loss of crypt architecture 3) Non-caseating granuloma … A) Ulcerative colitis B) Against ulcerative colitis C) Crohn's disease
questions.exp: Skip lesions argue against UC; cryptitis with loss of crypt architecture supports UC; non-caseating granulomas support Crohn's disease. (Book p35)

questions.q: Crohn's disease can occur:
opts: Anywhere from the oral cavity to the anal canal, including perianal disease
questions.exp: Site of involvement: can occur anywhere from oral cavity to anal canal (e.g. perianal involvement). (Book p35)

questions.q: Ileocolitis accounts for what proportion of Crohn's disease?
questions.exp: Ileocolitis: 40-50%. (Book p35)

questions.q: Ileitis alone accounts for what proportion of Crohn's disease?
questions.exp: Ileitis: 30-40%. (Book p35)

questions.q: Colitis alone accounts for what proportion of Crohn's disease?
questions.exp: Colitis: 15-20%. (Book p35)

questions.q: Match the Crohn's distribution to its printed frequency — 1) Ileocolitis 2) Ileitis 3) Colitis … A) 15-20% B) 30-40% C) 40-50%
questions.exp: Ileocolitis 40-50%; ileitis 30-40%; colitis 15-20%. (Book p35)

questions.q: The earliest macroscopic finding in Crohn's disease is:
questions.exp: Earliest finding: aphthous ulcers → small, translucent ulcers. (Book p35)

questions.q: The most visible macroscopic finding in Crohn's disease is:
questions.exp: Most visible finding: linear, serpiginous ulcers. (Book p35)

questions.q: The cobblestone appearance results from:
opts: Ulcers fusing longitudinally and transversely with areas of uninvolved mucosa between
questions.exp: Cobblestone appearance: the ulcers fuse longitudinally and transversely with areas of uninvolved mucosa in between. (Book p35)

questions.q: The macroscopic description of Crohn's lesions is:
questions.exp: Macroscopy: deep, transmural, asymmetric skip lesions. (Book p35)

questions.q: Thickening of the wall and strictures in Crohn's disease reflect:
opts: Transmural fibrosis and stenosis, typically in the terminal ileum
questions.exp: Thickening of the wall and strictures: transmural fibrosis and stenosis seen in terminal ileum. (Book p35)

questions.q: Creeping fat is thickened ____ encasing the bowel wall.
questions.exp: Creeping fat: thickened mesentery encasing the bowel wall. (Book p35)

questions.q: The garden hose appearance of the esophagus is noted in:
questions.exp: Note: garden hose appearance in esophagus → well developed progressive systemic sclerosis. (Book p35)

questions.q: At laparotomy for ileal Crohn's disease the surgeon finds the mesentery thickened and encasing the bowel wall. The book terms this:
questions.exp: Creeping fat: thickened mesentery encasing the bowel wall. (Book p35)

questions.q: Microscopically, Crohn's disease involves tissue up to the:
questions.exp: Microscopy: involvement up to muscularis propria. (Book p36)

questions.q: Non-caseating granulomas in Crohn's disease may be found:
opts: At any level and can be extraintestinal
questions.exp: Non-caseating granulomas: at any level, can be extraintestinal. (Book p36)

questions.q: The lymph node finding in Crohn's disease is:
questions.exp: Microscopy: mesenteric lymphadenopathy. (Book p36)

questions.q: Crypt architecture in Crohn's disease is:
questions.exp: Changes in crypts: cryptitis, crypt abscesses; crypt architecture — normal. (Book p36)

questions.q: Match the Crohn's microscopy item to its printed descriptor — 1) Crypt changes 2) Metaplasia 3) Aggregates 4) Deep involvement … A) Pyloric metaplasia B) Cryptitis and crypt abscesses with normal architecture C) Involvement up to muscularis propria D) Lymphoid aggregates
questions.exp: Cryptitis and crypt abscesses with normal crypt architecture; pyloric metaplasia; lymphoid aggregates; involvement up to muscularis propria. (Book p36)

questions.q: All of the following are listed causes of non-caseating granuloma EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Causes of non-caseating granuloma: sarcoidosis, tuberculosis, cat scratch disease, berylliosis, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, Crohn's disease. Rheumatoid arthritis is not listed. (Book p36)

questions.q: Which of these is listed among the causes of non-caseating granuloma?
questions.exp: Causes of non-caseating granuloma: sarcoidosis, tuberculosis, cat scratch disease, berylliosis, hypersensitivity pneumonitis, Crohn's disease. (Book p36)

questions.q: A resection specimen shows transmural inflammation with non-caseating granulomas and lymphoid aggregates, but crypt architecture is preserved. The book's diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Crohn's microscopy: involvement up to muscularis propria, non-caseating granulomas, lymphoid aggregates, cryptitis and crypt abscesses with normal crypt architecture. (Book p36)

units.title: Entities of IBD & Microscopic Colitis
units.guide:
Four entities are listed, but IBD currently means UC and CD only.
Microscopic colitis follows long-term PPI and NSAID use: chronic non-bloody voluminous watery diarrhea with a normal examination and normal endoscopy.
Biopsy: collagenous colitis (collagen band, Sjogren's) versus lymphocytic colitis (intra-epithelial lymphocytes, celiac disease).

units.title: Diversion Colitis & Normal Histology of Colon
units.sec: Diversion Colitis & Normal Histology of Colon
units.guide:
Diversion colitis occurs in patients using colostomy bags after surgery for bowel malignancies.
Normal colonic layers, innermost to outermost: mucosal epithelial cells, lamina propria, muscularis mucosa, submucosa, muscularis propria, serosa.
Learn the order — it anchors every depth-of-invasion comparison that follows.

units.title: Colonic Mucosa & Definition of Diarrhea
units.guide:
Colonic mucosa has no villi.
Crypts contain microvilli for water absorption; goblet cells secrete mucus.
Diarrhea is defined as a stool volume above 200 mL.

units.title: Epidemiology of UC and Crohn's Disease
units.sec: Epidemiology of UC and Crohn's Disease
units.guide:
Overall CD > UC and males > females; peaks at 15-30 and 70-90 years.
Ethnicity: Jews > non-Jewish white > African American > Hispanic > Asian.
Smoking protects against UC but causes CD; appendicectomy protects against UC; OCP raises CD risk; concordance is significant and greater in CD; antibiotics in the first year triple the risk.

units.title: Genetic Syndromes Associated with IBD
units.guide:
Childhood IBD is grouped as UC-like non-granulomatous versus CD-like granulomatous; Turner's syndrome is listed as most common.
Wiskott-Aldrich: WASP mutation, X-linked recessive, eczema plus sino-pulmonary infection plus microplatelet thrombocytopenia.
Hermansky-Pudlak: autosomal recessive with platelet dysfunction, pulmonary fibrosis and oculocutaneous albinism; von Gierke type I with glucose-1-phosphatase deficiency.

units.title: IPEX Syndrome & Early Onset Childhood IBD
units.sec: IPEX Syndrome & Early Onset Childhood IBD
units.guide:
Loss of Foxp3 function reduces regulatory T-cell tolerance and causes IPEX.
Triad: dermatitis, endocrinopathy (type I DM / thyroiditis) and UC-like enteropathy.
Supportive care, gene therapy and genetic testing; T-reg marker is CD25; early onset IBD reflects IL-10 pathway defects.

units.title: Pathogenesis of IBD
units.guide:
Exogenous and endogenous factors drive a dysregulated mucosal immune response in a genetically susceptible host.
UC: unclear pathogenesis with Th2 overactivity.
Crohn's: NOD2/CARD15 on chromosome 16, defective innate immunity (intracellular organisms, Paneth cell defensins), defective autophagy, Th1 overactivity and loss of protective Faecalibacterium.

units.title: Ulcerative Colitis: Site & Macroscopy
units.guide:
Rectum alone is involved in 50%.
Hemorrhagic, edematous, ulcerated granular mucosa with pseudopolyps from epithelial regeneration.
Chronic disease rarely gives a lead pipe atrophic featureless colon; fulminant colitis rarely gives toxic megacolon with a diameter above 6 cm.

units.title: Ulcerative Colitis: Microscopy
units.guide:
Cryptitis with loss of crypt architecture.
Paneth cell metaplasia distal to the hepatic flexure.
Basal plasma cells and lymphoid aggregates are the earliest finding and flag relapse; transmural disease, skip lesions, fistulas, strictures and fissures all argue against UC.

units.title: Crohn's Disease: Site & Macroscopy
units.guide:
Anywhere from mouth to anus; ileocolitis 40-50%, ileitis 30-40%, colitis 15-20%.
Deep transmural asymmetric skip lesions; aphthous ulcers are earliest, linear serpiginous ulcers most visible.
Cobblestoning, perianal fissures and fistulas, terminal ileal fibrosis and stenosis, and creeping fat.

units.title: Crohn's Disease: Microscopy
units.guide:
Involvement up to the muscularis propria with non-caseating granulomas at any level, even extraintestinal.
Mesenteric lymphadenopathy; cryptitis and crypt abscesses with normal crypt architecture.
Pyloric metaplasia, lymphoid aggregates and fibrosis; granuloma differential includes sarcoidosis, tuberculosis, cat scratch disease, berylliosis and hypersensitivity pneumonitis.
